Security of Critical Infrastructure Act 2018

Compilation C2026C00213 · in force; compilation No. 9 from 2026-06-04 · mandatory-for-scope · official text (free)

Applies to: Responsible entities for critical infrastructure assets.

s 1 Short titleStates the official short title of the Act. Coming soon
s 2 CommencementSets out when each provision of the Act starts, via a commencement table.
s 2(1) Provisions commence as the table's second column specifies, which also governs other statements there. Coming soon
s 2(2) Information in the table's third column is not law and may be edited. Coming soon
s 3 ObjectSets the Act's purpose: a framework for managing critical infrastructure risk, with several listed aims.
s 3(a) Aims to make ownership and operational control of critical infrastructure more transparent. Coming soon
s 3(b) Aims to encourage cooperation between governments, regulators, owners and operators on infrastructure risks. Coming soon
s 3(c) Aims to make responsible entities identify and manage risks to their assets. Coming soon
s 3(d) Aims to impose stronger cyber obligations on entities running systems of national significance. Coming soon
s 3(da) Aims to impose stronger security obligations on critical telecommunications asset entities. Coming soon
s 3(e) Aims to give the Commonwealth a regime for responding to serious infrastructure incidents. Coming soon
s 4 Simplified outline of this ActOverview of the framework: register, risk programs, incident notification, enhanced obligations, government powers and incident response. Coming soon
s 5 DefinitionsDefines terms used throughout the Act. Coming soon
s 5A Meaning of protected information and relevant informationDefines protected information and relevant information under the Act.
s 5A(1) Protected informationProtected information is relevant information whose disclosure could harm security, stability, or asset reliability, or is commercially confidential.
s 5A(1)(a) Covers information whose disclosure could prejudice national security or defence. Coming soon
s 5A(1)(b) Covers information whose disclosure could prejudice Australia's social or economic stability. Coming soon
s 5A(1)(c) Covers information that is or contains confidential commercial information. Coming soon
s 5A(1)(d) Covers information whose disclosure could harm an asset's availability, integrity, reliability or security. Coming soon
s 5A(2) Protected informationInformation is also protected if it met subsection (1) and was obtained by authorised disclosure.
s 5A(2)(a) Requires that the information met the protected information test in subsection (1). Coming soon
s 5A(2)(b) Requires that the person obtained it through an authorised disclosure or under section 46. Coming soon
s 5A(3) Relevant informationDefines relevant information as material obtained, generated or adopted in exercising or complying with the Act.
s 5A(3)(a) Includes material obtained or produced while exercising powers or duties under the Act. Coming soon
s 5A(3)(b) Includes material obtained, produced or adopted by an entity to comply with the Act. Coming soon
s 5A(3)(c) Includes records that an asset was declared a critical infrastructure asset. Coming soon
s 5A(3)(d) Includes records that an asset was declared a system of national significance. Coming soon
s 5A(3)(e) Includes records of the Minister giving or revoking a Ministerial authorisation.
s 5A(3)(e)(i) Includes records that a Ministerial authorisation was given. Coming soon
s 5A(3)(e)(ii) Includes records that a Ministerial authorisation was revoked. Coming soon
s 5A(3)(f) Includes an adopted critical infrastructure risk management program, or parts of it. Coming soon

s 6 Meaning of interest and control informationDefines the interest and control information an entity must give about an asset.
s 6(1) Lists the details counted as interest and control information about an entity and asset.
s 6(1)(a) Includes the first entity's name. Coming soon
s 6(1)(b) Includes the entity's ABN or equivalent foreign business number where applicable. Coming soon
s 6(1)(c) For non-individuals, includes head office address and country of formation.
s 6(1)(c)(i) Includes the head office or principal place of business address. Coming soon
s 6(1)(c)(ii) Includes the country where the entity was formed. Coming soon
s 6(1)(d) For individuals, includes residential address, country of residence and citizenship.
s 6(1)(d)(i) Includes the individual's residential address. Coming soon
s 6(1)(d)(ii) Includes the country where the individual usually lives. Coming soon
s 6(1)(d)(iii) Includes the individual's country or countries of citizenship. Coming soon
s 6(1)(e) Includes the type and level of interest held in the asset. Coming soon
s 6(1)(f) Includes information on the influence or control the entity can exercise over the asset. Coming soon
s 6(1)(g) Includes whether appointees to the governing body can directly access systems needed to run the asset. Coming soon
s 6(1)(h) Includes names of other entities able to influence or control the first entity.
s 6(1)(h)(i) Covers entities able to influence or control the first entity. Coming soon
s 6(1)(h)(ii) Covers entities able to influence or control entities already captured by this paragraph. Coming soon
s 6(1)(ha) Requires the same identity and control details for each higher controlling entity.
s 6(1)(ha)(i) Higher entities' identity details under paragraphs (b) to (e) are included. Coming soon
s 6(1)(ha)(ii) Includes the control a higher entity can exert over the first or other covered entities. Coming soon
s 6(1)(i) Includes any further information the rules prescribe. Coming soon
s 6(2) Interest and control information may include personal information under the Privacy Act. Coming soon
s 6(3) Interest and control information provided by States and TerritoriesState or Territory leaders who hold interests only through influence need not give interest and control information. Coming soon
s 6(4) Interest and control information provided by States and TerritoriesThe State or Territory itself must still report if it holds an interest under paragraph 8(1)(a) or (b). Coming soon
s 6(5) Interest and control information provided by the CommonwealthCommonwealth leaders holding an interest only through influence need not give interest and control information.

s 8 Meaning of direct interest holderDefines direct interest holder and its exemptions for lenders and custodians.
s 8(1) An entity is a direct interest holder with a 10% interest or one giving influence.
s 8(1)(a) Holding at least 10% of an asset, with associates, makes an entity a direct interest holder. Coming soon
s 8(1)(b) Holding any interest allowing direct or indirect influence or control makes an entity a direct interest holder. Coming soon
s 8(2) Exemption for moneylenders etc.Interests held solely as lending security, or from enforcing it, are exempt from subsection (1).
s 8(2)(a) Exemption requires the interest be held only as loan security or from enforcing it.
s 8(2)(a)(i) Interest held solely as security for a moneylending agreement. Coming soon
s 8(2)(a)(ii) Interest held solely from enforcing security for a moneylending agreement. Coming soon
s 8(2)(b) Exemption applies only to the lender, related parties, trustees or receivers listed.
s 8(2)(b)(i) The entity that entered into the moneylending agreement. Coming soon
s 8(2)(b)(ii) A subsidiary or holding entity of the lender. Coming soon
s 8(2)(b)(iii) A person able to determine the lender's investments or policy. Coming soon
s 8(2)(b)(iv) A security trustee holding the interest for the lender. Coming soon
s 8(2)(b)(v) A receiver appointed by or on instructions from the listed persons. Coming soon
s 8(3) Exemption for moneylenders etc.Defines a moneylending agreement as a good-faith commercial lending agreement or acquisition of its interest.
s 8(3)(a) Agreement made in good faith, on ordinary commercial terms, within a lending business. Coming soon
s 8(3)(b) Agreement by a lender or its holding entity to acquire an interest from such an agreement.
s 8(3)(b)(i) Applies where the entity itself carries on a moneylending business. Coming soon
s 8(3)(b)(ii) Applies where the entity is a subsidiary or holding entity of a lending corporation. Coming soon
s 8(4) Exemption for providers of custodial or depository servicesCustodial or depository service providers holding interests solely in that capacity, without influence, are exempt.
s 8(4)(a) Requires the entity to be a provider of custodial or depository services. Coming soon
s 8(4)(b) Requires the interest be held solely in the capacity of a custodial provider. Coming soon
s 8(4)(c) Custodial or depository exemption requires that holding the interest gives no ability to influence or control the asset. Coming soon
s 8(5) Exemption for providers of services specified in the rulesInterest held solely as a rules-specified service provider, without influence over the asset, is exempt.
s 8(5)(a) Exemption condition: the entity provides a service named in the rules. Coming soon
s 8(5)(b) Exemption condition: the interest is held only because the entity provides that service. Coming soon
s 8(5)(c) Exemption condition: holding the interest gives no direct or indirect power over the asset. Coming soon
s 8A Meaning of influence or controlDefines when an entity can influence or control an asset or another entity.
s 8A(1) Lists circumstances in which an entity is positioned to influence or control an asset.
s 8A(1)(a) Influence over an asset arises from voting or veto rights over its governing body. Coming soon
s 8A(1)(b) Influence arises from power to make decisions materially affecting the asset's operation or strategy. Coming soon
s 8A(1)(c) Influence arises from ability to appoint governing body members or key operating personnel.
s 8A(1)(c)(i) Ability to appoint members of the body governing the asset. Coming soon
s 8A(1)(c)(ii) Ability to appoint key personnel who run the asset. Coming soon
s 8A(1)(d) Influence arises from shaping decisions on plans, major spending, major contracts or major loans.
s 8A(1)(d)(i) Influence over the asset's business or other management plan. Coming soon
s 8A(1)(d)(ii) Influence over major expenditure concerning the asset. Coming soon
s 8A(1)(d)(iii) Influence over major contracts or transactions involving the asset. Coming soon
s 8A(1)(d)(iv) Influence over major loans involving the asset. Coming soon
s 8A(2) Lists circumstances in which one entity can influence or control another entity, including a 10% holding.
s 8A(2)(a) Control of another entity arises from voting or veto rights over it. Coming soon
s 8A(2)(b) Control arises from decisions materially affecting the other entity's running or strategy. Coming soon
s 8A(2)(c) Control arises from ability to appoint people to the other entity's board. Coming soon
s 8A(2)(d) Control arises from shaping decisions on plans, major spending, contracts or loans of the other entity.
s 8A(2)(d)(i) Influence over the other entity's business or management plan. Coming soon
s 8A(2)(d)(ii) Influence over major expenditure of the other entity. Coming soon
s 8A(2)(d)(iii) Influence over major contracts or transactions of the other entity. Coming soon
s 8A(2)(d)(iv) Influence over major loans involving the other entity. Coming soon
s 8A(2)(e) Holding at least ten percent in the other entity, with associates, counts as control. Coming soon
s 8A(3) The listed situations are not exhaustive of when influence or control exists. Coming soon
s 8B Meaning of associateDefines who counts as an associate of a person.
s 8B(a) A relative of the person is an associate. Coming soon
s 8B(b) Anyone acting, or planning to act, together with the person regarding an asset is an associate. Coming soon
s 8B(c) A business partner of the person is an associate. Coming soon
s 8B(d) A corporate entity where the person is a senior officer is an associate. Coming soon
s 8B(e) For a corporate person, its holding entities and senior officers are associates.
s 8B(e)(i) A corporate person's holding entity is an associate. Coming soon
s 8B(e)(ii) A corporate person's senior officer is an associate. Coming soon
s 8B(f) A company whose senior officers habitually follow the person's directions is an associate.
s 8B(f)(i) Company whose senior officers follow the person's wishes or instructions. Coming soon
s 8B(f)(ii) Company whose senior officers follow the directions of a corporate person's senior officers. Coming soon
s 8B(g) A company whose directions the person is accustomed or obliged to follow is an associate.
s 8B(g)(i) Person is accustomed or obliged to follow the corporate entity's directions. Coming soon
s 8B(g)(ii) Person is accustomed or obliged to follow the corporate entity's senior officers. Coming soon
s 8B(h) A body corporate in which the person holds an interest is an associate. Coming soon
s 8B(i) For a body corporate person, anyone holding an interest in it is an associate. Coming soon
s 8B(j) The trustee of a trust in which the person has an interest is an associate. Coming soon
s 8B(k) For a trustee person, anyone with an interest in the trust is an associate. Coming soon
s 8B(l) Others prescribed by the rules are also associates. Coming soon
s 8C Meanings of subsidiary and holding entityDefines subsidiary and holding entity relationships between corporate entities.
s 8C(1) Meaning of subsidiaryA company is a subsidiary if another controls majority votes or securities, or via a chain.
s 8C(1)(a) Subsidiary status arises from majority voting power or majority of issued securities.
s 8C(1)(a)(i) Higher entity can control over half the voting power in the lower entity. Coming soon
s 8C(1)(a)(ii) Higher entity holds over half the lower entity's issued securities, ignoring limited-participation ones. Coming soon
s 8C(1)(b) A subsidiary of a subsidiary is also a subsidiary, through repeated application. Coming soon
s 8C(2) Meaning of holding entityA company is a holding entity of any company that is its subsidiary. Coming soon

s 30AH Critical infrastructure risk management programDefines the risk management program as a written program with hazard-focused purposes.

s 30AH(4)(d)(ii) Identity verification option: an in-person check. Coming soon

s 50 Simplified outline of this PartOutline: Minister may privately declare assets critical, notify reporting entities, and disclosure is an offence. Coming soon
s 51 Declaration of assets by the MinisterMinister may declare an asset critical, naming the responsible entity and notifying reporting entities within 30 days.
s 51(1) Minister may formally designate an extra asset as critical infrastructure when stated conditions are satisfied.
s 51(1)(a) Declaration only possible for assets not already covered as critical infrastructure. Coming soon
s 51(1)(b) Asset must be connected to one of the recognised critical infrastructure sectors. Coming soon
s 51(1)(c) Minister must be satisfied the asset matters to economic stability, defence or security.
s 51(1)(c)(i) Asset's importance may relate to Australia's social or economic stability. Coming soon
s 51(1)(c)(ii) Asset's importance may relate to Australia's defence. Coming soon
s 51(1)(c)(iii) Asset's importance may relate to national security. Coming soon
s 51(1)(d) Disclosure of the asset's status must pose a risk to stability, defence or security.
s 51(1)(d)(i) Public knowledge of status could endanger social or economic stability. Coming soon
s 51(1)(d)(ii) Public knowledge of status could endanger Australia's defence. Coming soon
s 51(1)(d)(iii) Public knowledge of status could endanger national security. Coming soon
s 51(2) Declaration must name which entity is responsible for the asset. Coming soon
s 51(2A) Declaration may switch on Part 2, 2A or 2B obligations for the asset.
s 51(2A)(a) Declaration may apply Part 2 to the asset. Coming soon
s 51(2A)(b) Declaration may apply Part 2A to the asset. Coming soon
s 51(2A)(c) Declaration may apply Part 2B to the asset. Coming soon
s 51(3) Minister must give written notice of the declaration within thirty days to specified parties.
s 51(3)(a) Notice of declaration goes to each reporting entity for the asset. Coming soon
s 51(3)(b) For located tangible assets, the relevant State or Territory leader must be notified. Coming soon
s 51(5) Such a declaration is not a legislative instrument. Coming soon
s 51A Consultation—declarationMinister must consult the named responsible entity before declaring, allowing submissions and giving reasons.
s 51A(1) Minister must give entity notice of proposed declaration inviting submissions within set period.
s 51A(1)(a) The notice must set out the proposed declaration. Coming soon
s 51A(1)(b) The notice must invite submissions within twenty-eight days or a shorter specified period.
s 51A(1)(b)(i) Default submission window is twenty-eight days from notice. Coming soon
s 51A(1)(b)(ii) Notice may instead specify a shorter submission period. Coming soon
s 51A(2) Minister must consider submissions received within the applicable period.
s 51A(2)(a) Submissions received within the standard twenty-eight day period must be considered. Coming soon
s 51A(2)(b) Submissions received within any shorter specified period must be considered. Coming soon
s 51A(3) Shorter submission period allowed only where urgent circumstances make it necessary. Coming soon
s 51A(4) Notice must state reasons, unless that would harm security. Coming soon
s 52 Notification of change to reporting entities for assetReporting entities must tell the Secretary of changes in who the reporting entities are.
s 52(1) Section applies when a reporting entity stops being one or learns of another.
s 52(1)(a) Triggered when the entity ceases to be a reporting entity. Coming soon
s 52(1)(b) Triggered when the entity learns of another reporting entity for the asset. Coming soon
s 52(2) Entity must notify the Secretary within thirty days; civil penalty applies.
s 52(2)(a) Notification must state the triggering fact, either cessation or awareness of another. Coming soon
s 52(2)(b) Notification must give other entities' names and head office addresses, as far as known. Coming soon
s 52(3) Entity must make best efforts to find other entities' names and addresses. Coming soon
s 52(4) Secretary must tell newly notified entities of the declaration within thirty days. Coming soon

s 52B(1)(b) Minister must be satisfied the asset is nationally significant. Coming soon

s 52B(2)(a)(ii) Consequences for defence of Australia are considered. Coming soon

s 52C(1)(a) The notice must set out the proposed declaration. Coming soon
s 52C(1)(b) Notice must invite submissions within twenty-eight days or a shorter specified period.

s 52C(1)(b)(ii) Notice may specify a shorter submission period. Coming soon

s 52C(2)(a) Submissions within the standard twenty-eight day period must be considered. Coming soon

s 54(1) The Act treats a partnership as an entity, subject to modifications. Coming soon
s 54(2) Partnership obligations fall on each partner, dischargeable by any one. Coming soon
s 54(3) Partnership offences are attributed to each partner involved in the act or omission.
s 54(3)(a) Partner who personally did the act or omission is liable. Coming soon
s 54(3)(b) Partner who helped or induced the act or omission is liable. Coming soon
s 54(3)(c) Partner knowingly involved in the act or omission is liable. Coming soon
s 54(4) Same attribution rules apply to civil penalty contraventions. Coming soon
s 54(5) Changes in a partnership's membership do not break its continuity. Coming soon

s 55(2) Trusts or superannuation funds with a single trusteeWith a sole trustee, obligations and offences fall on that trustee.
s 55(2)(a) Single trustee bears the trust's obligations. Coming soon
s 55(2)(b) Single trustee is treated as committing the trust's offences. Coming soon
s 55(3) Trusts or superannuation funds with multiple trusteesWith several trustees, obligations bind each and offences attach to those involved.
s 55(3)(a) Each trustee bears the obligations, which any one trustee may discharge. Coming soon
s 55(3)(b) Offences are attributed to each trustee who acted, assisted or was knowingly involved.
s 55(3)(b)(i) Trustee who personally did the act or omission is liable. Coming soon
s 55(3)(b)(ii) Trustee who helped or induced the act or omission is liable. Coming soon
s 55(3)(b)(iii) Trustee knowingly involved in the act or omission is liable. Coming soon

s 56(2) Obligations of such a company fall on each appointed officer, and any one may discharge them. Coming soon
s 56(3) Appointed officers are deemed to commit the company's offence if they acted, assisted or were knowingly involved.
s 56(3)(a) An officer who personally did the act or made the omission is liable. Coming soon
s 56(3)(b) An officer who aided, abetted, counselled or procured the act or omission is liable. Coming soon
s 56(3)(c) An officer knowingly concerned in or party to the act or omission is liable. Coming soon
s 56(4) Civil penalty contraventions are handled like offences under this section on foreign companies. Coming soon

s 60AA Compensation for acquisition of propertyThe Commonwealth owes reasonable compensation for property acquired on unjust terms; courts can decide disputes.

s 60AA(2) If compensation is not agreed, the entity may sue in a federal or state court.

Reuse: Official Australian Government text, free to read; reuse terms in the publisher's terms of use (not re-checked); cite IDs and paraphrase. Only identifiers, links and headings are shown, never the text; every summary and note is our own.

The sloptopop CLI and every language library are open source under MIT OR Apache-2.0, at github.com/sloptopop.

Transformations, A to Z: every step from the repository you start with to the branch you get back.

Slop to pop: design patterns: anti-patterns sloptopop converts into design patterns today, with the run that proves each one.

Results: what sloptopop did to every repository it was tested on.

Compliance, point by point and what each check evidences: what sloptopop checks and which controls each check evidences.

This site runs no JavaScript except htmx on the pricing page, to send the waitlist form; every animation is CSS. No cookies, no analytics, no third-party scripts.
